Figure_3.mapping: Rows H1, H2, H3 correspond exactly to primary.json contrasts.
Figure_3.caption: Prespecified patient-level contrasts. Points show differences in percentage points; horizontal bars show original two-sided 95% Newcombe method 10 confidence intervals. H1 compares Method A low-quality detection in the BrEaST external test cohort with the BUS-BRA internal holdout. H2 compares Method A simulated review fractions between those cohorts. H3 compares low-quality detection for Method B minus Method A among the same 16 external low-quality patients and uses the original paired interval. H2 and H3 intervals are nominal without multiplicity adjustment. Low quality is Dice <0.70. Numerators and denominators are shown for each contrast.

Figure_4.mapping: A=BUS-BRA internal holdout; B=BrEaST external test; C=primary H3 and supplementary external_equal_review.detection_B_minus_A.
Figure_4.caption: Risk-ranked review curves and external paired contrasts. Panels A and B show empirical step curves of the fraction of low-quality patients detected versus the actual number selected for simulated review, ranked by descending risk with official CaseID as the lexicographic tie-breaker. The cohorts contain 93/851 and 16/252 low-quality patients, respectively (Dice <0.70). Blue solid and orange dashed curves represent Methods A and B. Filled squares mark the development-locked cutoffs (internal A: 71/93 detected at 174 reviews; B: 68/93 at 150; external A: 10/16 at 35; B: 13/16 at 33). Open circles mark 50 external reviews per method (A: 14/16; B: 13/16). Panel C shows B minus A detection differences with the original paired nominal 95% Newcombe method 10 intervals: +18.75 [−4.28, +40.04] percentage points at locked cutoffs and −6.25 [−31.61, +19.57] at top 50. The latter interval conditions on the observed ranking and does not account for re-ranking in another sample.

Figure_S1.mapping: A=external-minus-internal Method A detection; B=external B-minus-A paired detection. Each panel uses Dice cutoffs 0.50, 0.70, 0.80, with 0.70 from primary.json and other cutoffs from supplementary.json.
Figure_S1.caption: Sensitivity to the Dice definition of low quality with development-locked risk cutoffs unchanged. Panel A shows Method A detection in the BrEaST external test minus BUS-BRA internal holdout. Panel B shows paired Method B minus Method A detection in BrEaST. Low-quality denominators for Dice <0.50, <0.70, and <0.80 are 53, 93, and 183 internally and 7, 16, and 50 externally. Points show the original differences in percentage points and bars the original nominal two-sided 95% Newcombe method 10 confidence intervals. No interval was replaced by a bootstrap interval.

Figure_S2.mapping: A=primary.cohorts.external_test.paired_low_quality; B=supplementary.external_equal_review.paired_low_quality. Bar counts independently derived from actual validation records.
Figure_S2.caption: Paired detection outcomes for the same 16 BrEaST external low-quality patients (Dice <0.70), under two review policies. Panel A uses development-locked cutoffs: both methods detect 10 patients, Method A only 0, Method B only 3, and neither 3; the corresponding review counts are 35/252 for A and 33/252 for B. Panel B uses the top 50 ranked patients per method: both detect 12, A only 2, B only 1, and neither 1. The four mutually exclusive outcome categories sum to 16 under each policy. Counts were derived from the archived patient-level flags and deterministic ranking, not read from a previous graphic. The locked-cutoff A-only cell has zero observed support.
